name: Polish
modelReview: Usage notes written in Polish 2026-11-13 by a writer told nothing of cron; answers, lexicon and hand-written rows by Claude Fable 5.2, parked that day after two schedule reads and two blind reads. Resumed 2026-11-19: four author passes against one adversarial schedule read of all 705 rows and three blind readers briefed only in Polish asked for every reading. Renderer built by an agent that saw no other renderer and no held-out row: 152 of 153 held-out rows on the first judged run (the miss settled for the row: an unbroken rhythm across the hours is one step between its first and last firing). Audited by an independent agent (about 870 sentences and all 662 rows read against the answer key): no wrong schedule; two forms of wrong Polish and the continuity declaration repaired test-first. Orthography checked against sources actually opened (CLDR 48, pl.wikipedia, zpe.gov.pl); PWN and RJP could not be opened; comma rules unverified. The forms the audit changed were read only by its own four readers, whose isolation is uncertain. Thin evidence or known heavy forms: «chwili wypadającej …»; «godziny parzyste» (one attestation); «w godzinach rozpoczynających się o …» (two of three readers reported a second reading); ten windows for many separate hours under a rhythm of minutes; stacked exceptions; whether hour12 should exist. Taste calls (Claude Fable 5.2) are in in the answers with their evidence. Reading check 2026-11-19 (tooling/scripts/reading): all 726 conformance rows read by three Sonnet 5.5 readers briefed only in Polish, 5,249 questions about moments scored against the independent answer key, 99.94% of answers right; no question was misread by most readers, so none needed a recheck; ten were missed by one reader each (five of them on «co 4 lata od 2028 r.: …» and on «od 9:10 do 17:40: co minutę od 10 do 40 minut po …»), notes only. After the cost pass of 2026-11-19 every other hour of the whole day is said by parity at any minute («o każdej nieparzystej godzinie», «30 minut po każdej parzystej godzinie»; the even hours on the hour stay «co 2 godziny»), and the missing minute «chwili wypadającej …» was looked at again and kept; the reading check then read all 735 rows (5,328 questions, three readers) with one question misread by two of three readers («2, 22 i 42 minuty po każdej pełnej godzinie» at 23:42), which every one of six readers of two models answered rightly when asked alone, so no defect.
